Not sick. Not obviously lame. Just not quite right — and the clock knows it before the rider does.

Dr. Leo works with performance horses in DFW whose owners are done guessing. One visit tells you whether what you're feeling is a training gap or something that needs to be adjusted out.

Most of the time, it's both. The adjustment comes first.

If your horse is in the middle of a hard season and something feels off, don't wait until it costs you a run.

DM us to book.

This is the stretch that separates horses that finish the season strong from the ones that start falling apart in September.

Most performance horses in North Texas have been hauling, running, and working since the ground was still cool. That adds up — in their backs, their necks, and the joints nobody thinks to check.

Dr. Leo is mobile. He comes to your barn, evaluates your horse where he lives, and adjusts what needs to move.

No trailer stress. No fighting a sore horse into a stock trailer.
